conclusions: Both paired cases completed from physically generated shared first proposals in separately owned sessions. DIRECT_REPAIR and DIRECT_MODEL_REPAIR each accepted zero of two first or later solutions; every stage reached unchanged exact acceptance.
All ten physical calls delivered complete JSON with known usage, no provider failure, retry, truncation, schema or authority failure. The failures are not attributable to unstable transport.

The independent counts-only observer classified all ten allocated certificate proposals as AS_WRITTEN_NUMERIC_MISMATCH. None contained a canonical match, mathematically equivalent noncanonical value, unclassified text or malformed certificate. Twenty-five allocated output values were wrong; shared-prefix replays mean these are twenty distinct physically generated values, not twenty-five independent values.

The interpolation public formulation met the unchanged structural contract and was actually supplied to the next call, which still produced wrong values. Structural admission does not validate the equations; their mathematical appropriateness was not independently graded or retained.

The passive-network formulation bound the correct problem and met object, assumption and byte checks, but returned zero equations for three required outputs. Its measured reasons were EQUATION_COUNT and OUTPUT_LABEL_SET, not a provider, syntax or security refusal.

Each arm used six allocated calls; the two common first proposals were physically generated once and fully charged to both arms. Twelve allocated calls and 30834 tokens correspond to ten physical calls and 25309 tokens; the 5525 shared-prefix tokens are explicit.

Treatment used 14224 allocated tokens versus 16610 control and no more model compute in both pairs; neither pair matched the five-percent realized whole-stage or repair-only token tolerance. Lower cost with no accepted solutions is not a cognitive or efficiency gain.

Two new parameter cases in two already-known families constitute a focused diagnostic, not fresh cross-domain transfer, an official benchmark score or recursive-improvement evidence. Prior negative epochs remain unchanged.
